name: Rooted-Wedge Membership and Forbidden-Minor Classification
statement: Let $(A,a)$ and $(B,b)$ be pointed cover-recursively peripheral partial cubes. Their one-point amalgam $A\vee B$ belongs to the class exactly when at least one factor has a root-avoiding decomposition. If both factors are nontrivial, the wedge is periphery-free exactly when both roots are locked, and it is a forbidden pc-minor exactly when both pointed factors are root-critical. Consequently the one-vertex-decomposable forbidden pc-minors are precisely the wedges of two nontrivial root-critical pointed members.
proof: A root-avoiding decomposition peels its factor inside the wedge because every removed side omits the attachment vertex. Conversely, the first peripheral coordinate of a recursive wedge decomposition lies in one factor and its peripheral side must avoid the common root; induction either completes a root-avoiding decomposition of that factor or supplies one in the other. The same section calculation makes wedge peripherality equivalent to an avoiding periphery in a factor. Root-criticality repairs every root-side restriction and contraction, so all elementary wedge minors return to the class; minimality of a forbidden wedge forces the converse conditions on both factors.
